```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
library(tidyverse)
library(readr)
```

```{r}
salaries <- read_csv(paste0(
  "https://stat.cmu.edu/~sgallagh/courses/mads-fall-2026/",
  "datavis-36613/data/salaries.csv.gz"
))

duplicate_rows <- salaries[duplicated(salaries), ]
duplicate_df <- as.data.frame(duplicate_rows)
duplicate_df[1,]
duplicate_df[3,]

duplicate_counts <- duplicate_df %>% count(across(everything()), sort = TRUE)
head(duplicate_counts, n = 10)

salaries$experience_level <- factor(
  salaries$experience_level,
  levels = c("EX", "SE", "MI", "EN"),
  labels = c("Executive", "Senior", "Mid", "Entry")
)
```

```{r}
salaries |> 
  group_by(work_year) |> 
  summarise(n = n())

exp <- salaries |> 
  filter(
    employment_type == "FT"
  ) |> 
  group_by(experience_level, work_year) |> 
  summarize(
    median_salary = median(salary_in_usd, na.rm = TRUE),
    n = n(), 
    .groups = "drop"
  )


ggplot(exp, aes(
  x = work_year, 
  y = median_salary, 
  color = experience_level,
  group = experience_level
)) +
  geom_line() + 
  geom_point() +
  labs(
    title = "Median Full-Time Salary by Experience Levels, 2020-2025",
    subtitle = "(in USD)",
    x = "Work Year",
    y = "Median Annual Salary (USD)",
    color = "Experience Level",
    caption = paste(
      "Subset: Full-Time Employees Only\n",
      "Limitations: Some experience-level/year combinations have",
      "relatively few observations, so their medians and trends should",
      "be interpreted with caution."
    )
  ) + 
  theme_classic()

hist(salaries$salary_in_usd)
```
```{r}
library(plotly)

salaries_grouped <- salaries |> 
  filter(
    employment_type == "FT"
  ) |> 
  group_by(experience_level, work_year) |> 
  summarise(count = n(), 
            average_salary = mean(salary_in_usd))
fig <- salaries_grouped %>%
  plot_ly(
    x = ~ average_salary, 
    #y = ~count, 
    size = ~count, 
    color = ~experience_level, 
    frame = ~work_year, 
    text = ~paste(
      "Experience Level:", experience_level,
      "<br>Count:", count,
      "<br>Average Salary: $", format(round(average_salary, 2), big.mark = ",", nsmall = 2)
    ),
    hoverinfo = "text",
    type = 'scatter',
    mode = 'markers',
    marker = list(
      sizemode = "diameter",
      sizeref = 0.9
    )
  )
fig <- fig %>% layout(
    xaxis = list(
      type = "log"
    )
  )
fig <- fig %>%
  animation_opts(
    1000, easing = "elastic", redraw = FALSE
  )

fig
```

```{r}
library(stringr)
salaries_count <- salaries |> 
  group_by(job_title) |> 
  summarise(count = n()) |> 
  arrange(desc(count))
example <- salaries |> 
  filter(str_detect(job_title, "BI"))
table(example$job_title)

example2 <- salaries |> 
  filter(str_detect(job_title, "Quant"))
table(example2$job_title)

salaries_family_base <- salaries |> 
  mutate(
    role_family = case_when(
      
      str_detect(job_title, "Data Scie") ~ "Data Science",
      str_detect(job_title, "Data Engin") ~ "Data Engineering",
      str_detect(job_title, "Data Analy") ~ "Data Analyst",
      str_detect(job_title, "Software Eng") ~ "Software Engineer",
      TRUE ~ "Other")
  )
table(salaries_family_base$role_family)

#how to do ai
salaries_family_more <- salaries |> 
  mutate(
    role_family = case_when(
      
      str_detect(job_title, "Data Scie") ~ "Data Science",
      str_detect(job_title, "Data Engin") ~ "Data Engineering",
      str_detect(job_title, "Data Analy") ~ "Data Analyst",
      str_detect(job_title, "Software Eng") ~ "Software Engineer",
      str_detect(job_title, "Machine Learning") ~ "Machine Learning",
      str_detect(job_title, regex("BI|Business Intelligence", ignore_case = TRUE)) ~ "Business Intelligence",
      TRUE ~ "Other")
  )
table(salaries_family_more$role_family)


```
